title: Complex Fuchsian rigidity of ball quotients with critical exponent two and a compact positive-dimensional analytic subset
source_title: Holomorphic functions on geometrically finite quotients of the ball
author: William Sarem
difficulty_reason: The prior existence and contraction formulas for the natural flow do not themselves force a quotient containing a compact analytic set to preserve a complex geodesic. The authored proof uses calibrated volume minimality to rule out strict contraction, turns trace equality on every limit-set direction into a single complex tangent line, and then localizes the analytic set in the invariant geodesic quotient. Showing that this quotient must be compact supplies the global rigidity obligation beyond the precise prior flow and comparison foundations.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Discrete torsion-free subgroup Gamma of PU(n,1), complex hyperbolic metric normalized with sectional curvatures between minus four and minus one, critical exponent exactly two, and a compact positive-dimensional closed analytic subset in the ball quotient. Then Gamma preserves a complex geodesic and acts cocompactly on it. Full primary equality-case proof26–27 and new Patterson–Sullivan differential/Hessian/Levi calculation11–12 read, with invariant density support9 and convex confinement Proposition1.1 on10–11. Elementary exclusions13–14 and complex analytic definitions6–8 included. Named Busemann regularity and comparison, Patterson–Sullivan existence and maximum principle are published background. No geometrical finiteness or convex-cocompact assumption added; no inference that all exponent-two quotients are Fuchsian.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author studies the equality case of a Patterson–Sullivan Levi-form inequality, forces all limit-set directions into one complex tangent line, and deduces preservation and cocompactness of a complex geodesic. This critical-exponent Kähler rigidity exceeds ordinary qualifying exams.
